summary: The legacy project has 40 original static SVG figures (one per manifest entry, chapters 0-24). They come from one Python generator (scripts/figures.py, about 540 lines, no dependencies) that computes coordinates from real formulas. A second pass (scripts/typeset-figures.mjs) swaps 226 exact-string labels for MathJax vector glyphs using content/figure-math.json and rewrites hex colours into a five-role light/dark CSS-variable palette. A Playwright checker (scripts/check-figures.mjs) renders all 40 in both themes and fails on clipped, overlapping, stroke-crossed or overpainted labels; the latest report shows 80 renders, 0 issues. I regenerated the manifest from figures.py in the scratchpad and it matches the committed one, so the pipeline is reproducible. I viewed every current light capture (qa/figure-*-light.png, 2026-09-09 23:00), several dark and phone-width captures, and the history and Earth screenshots. Science is careful throughout. I re-derived the GPS net gain GM/c^2(1/R - 3/(2r)) (+38.5 us/day, crossover at h = R/2), the tossed-clock +89.2/-44.6/+44.6 as, the Earth tidal gradient 2GM/r^3 = 3.08e-6 s^-2, the Eddington-Finkelstein cone slopes (r - rs)/(r + rs), the Newtonian calibration of kappa, the horizon-area bound 1 - 1/sqrt2, the Raychaudhuri focusing bound and the 30-degree Cartan holonomy inset. All are correct, and every caption states its approximation and exaggeration. Visually the set is uneven, and it all uses one 1000-unit landscape slide template: numbered uppercase heading, coloured headline and subtitle, diagram on the left and prose on the right. The strongest figures are single geometric constructions with a visible invariant: light cone, affine-parameter dots, action variation, lapse/shift, black-hole radii to scale, horizon-area disks, wave polarizations and the rebuilt Cartan plane/sphere comparison. The weakest are boxed-formula cards and flowcharts that belong in HTML/KaTeX: Newtonian calibration, product rule, constraint count, calculation map, effective theory. Only 7 of 40 have a phone composition (data-mobile-viewbox); the rest shrink to about 7 px labels in a 350 px column. The four public-domain history images (Newton 1689, Principia 1687, Einstein 1921, Einstein 1916 title page) and the NASA Blue Marble Earth texture ship with exemplary provenance manifests (source, licence rationale, modifications, sha256, verification date) and can be reused verbatim. Six review docs give specific, evidence-linked critique of every figure, but they overlap and go stale fast (visual-review.md still lists superseded titles and captions). second-figure-review.md (2026-09-09) is the most current disposition. For grbook.ai: reuse the formulas, captions and limitation statements, the palette roles, the provenance schema and the label-collision test idea. Rebuild most figures as Svelte/KaTeX components, turning about 15 into interactive demos. Drop the Python/MathJax string-matching pipeline.
lessons_learned: Do not bake prose into SVG. The shared 1000x480 template (a 'NN / TITLE' heading, then a headline and subtitle, then diagram left and prose right) made the collection read like lecture slides. At a 350 px phone column a 20-unit label renders at about 7 px (docs/figure-aesthetic-review-01-20.md). Only 7 of 40 figures got a data-mobile-viewbox composition. In grbook.ai keep titles, captions and explanations in responsive HTML, keep only construction labels inside the drawing, and design the phone layout first.

Author math labels as TeX at the source. content/figure-math.json maps exact display strings to TeX. It has drifted: 24 of 226 keys match no current label, and '1912-13' is unmapped, so it renders visibly in sans-serif among serif dates on the historical timeline (qa/figure-historical-timeline-light.png). In Svelte, pass TeX straight to KaTeX instead of post-matching strings.

Keep build passes idempotent. scripts/typeset-figures.mjs rewrites the SVGs in place (prefixes IDs, replaces text with glyphs, maps hex colours to CSS variables), so it is only correct immediately after figures.py regenerates the files. Keep sources and outputs separate.

Automated layout checks are necessary but not sufficient. check-figures.mjs catches clipping, overlap, label/stroke collisions and overpainting (80/80 pass), but it passed boundary-variation after its dashed tangents were thinned until they almost disappear into the curve. The figure's whole point is now barely visible in qa/figure-boundary-variation-light.png. Pair every automated pass with a visual review against the question 'can the reader point at the part of the image that justifies the caption?' (docs/figure-aesthetic-review-21-40.md).

One colour means one role, everywhere. The five-role palette (geometry teal, curvature violet, transport blue, matter amber, observer rose, with dark variants above 4.5:1 contrast) is worth keeping. The figures that confused readers broke it: polar-metric draws r in rose but labels r dtheta teal while listing 'Angular: r dtheta' in rose; the three Rindler hyperbolae are coloured but unlabelled; the cosmic-expansion legend runs in reverse vertical order to the curves.

Spacetime diagrams need equal ct and x scales. Two legacy figures silently use unequal pixel scales: Rindler (105 px vs 85 px per unit, so the null asymptote sits at about 39 degrees) and horizon-cones (ingoing null rays not at 45 degrees). The light-cone figure gets it right. Make an equal-scale axis helper the default in grbook.ai.

Compute annotations from the same model as the curves. figures.py computes every curve from a formula, but tangents, edge labels, reference lines and axis scales are typed in as pixel literals, and that is exactly where the surviving defects are: the boundary-variation tangent about 10% shallower than the real slope, polar-metric's 'dr' beside an angular arc, the light-bending ray 5 px off its own reference line, and the 39-degree and 55-degree 'null' lines in Rindler and horizon-cones. In grbook.ai, derive tangents, labels and anchors from the model object, and unit-test anchor positions (for example, a tangent slope equals the derivative) rather than only testing label collisions.

Keep the honesty rule: every figure is computed from a stated model and its caption names the approximation, the exaggeration and what the picture does not show. It stopped several classic misconceptions: caustic is not a singularity, Hubble radius is not a horizon, the area theorem is a bound not an efficiency, Flamm-style radii are not proper distances. Carry this into the grbook.ai figure spec.

Boxed formula cards and process flowcharts (connection-cancellation before its rebuild, newtonian-calibration, action-product-rule, constraint-count, calculation-map, effective-theory) were consistently the weakest figures in three separate reviews. Derivations belong in aligned KaTeX with colour roles. Checklists belong in HTML or as an AI-tutor tool, not in illustrations.

Give each idea one primary representation. Once an interactive existed, the legacy build demoted the static SVG to a collapsed 'reference diagram' or a 'Diagram' tab (build-site.mjs chapterFigure / referenceByLesson / paired scenes). Before that, figure and scene competed as duplicate introductions (docs/visualization-audit.md). Plan interactive and static fallback as a pair from the start.

Show visual claims directly in the picture. The two most effective late fixes were geometric: caustic paths continuing past the focus, and the Page curve sharing its early branch with the semiclassical trend (docs/second-figure-review.md). No added prose achieved the same.

Reuse the media provenance schema. assets/history/manifest.json and assets/earth/manifest.json record source page, direct file URL, author and date, licence and jurisdiction rationale, upstream and local modifications, pixel size, sha256 and a verification date. Adopt it for every grbook.ai image, texture and video.

Keep a single source of truth for status. Six overlapping review docs recorded dispositions on 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-09 that were superseded within hours (figures 06, 12, 14, 18, 35, 36 and 38 changed after being reviewed). Track figure status in the knowledge vault, not parallel markdown reviews.

Do not identify figures by ordinal. figures.py re-sorts by (chapter, after) and rewrites the 'NN /' heading, so the number is a global position, not a chapter (Rindler '09' is in chapter 5), and adding one figure shifts every later number. The review docs cite figures as '15', '22', '35'. Key status, reviews and cross-links on stable ids such as polar-metric.

assets.title: 01 A derivative predicts the next small step
assets.teaches: Uses a cart with x = 3t^2 to show that the tangent line at t = 2 s (x = 12 m, v = 12 m/s) matches value and slope, predicting the next small displacement dx = v dt, while the curve keeps accelerating. This is the first-order/second-order hierarchy the book later reuses for local expansions of the metric.
assets.pedagogy: Concrete units first (metres, seconds), then the approximation symbol. Placed as the chapter 0 opener for novices.
assets.physics_model: Exact parabola x = (3 m/s^2) t^2 and tangent x = 12t - 12, plotted from the formulas.

strengths: Correct and uncluttered; the contact label has a leader and clears both curves
One of 7 figures with a dedicated phone composition
Dashed tangent vs solid curve reads instantly
issues: Right column is a mini-article (headline, rule, equation, two sentences) that shrinks the plot
Does not show the growing gap between line and curve, which is the actual lesson about error order

assets.pedagogy: Split comparison, one laboratory vs two. The caption warns that drawn curvature of coordinate worldlines is not evidence of spacetime curvature.
assets.physics_model: Schematic only: separation shrinks quadratically in time (70 - 35 (i/50)^2 in drawing units). No physical scale.

strengths: Conceptually right framing: relative acceleration is the observable
Honest caption about coordinate schematics
issues: Visually thin: a near-straight line with a dot, and a right panel that reads as an arch
No measured separations on common time slices and no drawn instruments
Axes have no scale; large empty panels and a centre divider

assets.pedagogy: Side-by-side arrow and level-set pictures. The caption notes that rescaling a coordinate changes both components but leaves the pairing invariant. In the legacy book it was the 'Diagram' tab of a 3D covector-planes scene.
assets.physics_model: Exact: evenly spaced lines x = 0..4, vector from origin to (3,2).

strengths: Concrete counting interpretation of a one-form
Strong, confident arrows; equal-weight comparison
issues: Left panel's rose projection arrow is unlabelled
The arrowhead lands exactly on the x = 3 line; crossed intervals are not highlighted, so the reader counts boundaries instead of intervals
The invariance under rescaling is claimed in the caption but not shown

assets.title: 05 The minus sign creates a light cone
assets.teaches: In 1+1 Minkowski spacetime with equal x and ct scales, light rays (|dx| = c dt) bound the future of an event. A massive observer's displacement is timelike, inside the cone; a spacelike displacement is outside.
assets.pedagogy: One generous construction and a restrained fill. Paired in the legacy book with a 2+1 3D cone scene.
assets.physics_model: Exact 45-degree null lines on equal-scale axes.

strengths: Equal-scale axes (unlike the Rindler and horizon-cone figures)

Flat truncation of the fill at the top; heavy arrowheads
No invariant-interval readout or boost

assets.teaches: The home clock takes 10 years on a vertical worldline. A traveller at 0.6c to 3 light-years and back accumulates 10 sqrt(1 - 0.6^2) = 8 years. Same departure and reunion events, different spacetime lengths.
assets.pedagogy: Shared endpoint events emphasised. The caption notes the proper-time integral, not a 'feeling' of slow time, gives the difference, and that the sharp turnaround is idealised.

assets.title: 07 Coordinates are not rulers (polar metric)
assets.teaches: A polar grid on the flat plane has radial edge dr and angular edge r dtheta, so ds^2 = dr^2 + r^2 dtheta^2 and the cell area is about r dr dtheta. Grid lines can curve while the surface stays flat.
assets.pedagogy: An enlarged annular cell with physical edge lengths. In the legacy book it was a collapsed reference inside the interactive shrinking-cell polar-metric lesson.
assets.physics_model: Exact polar grid; the finite cell is enlarged for visibility (stated in the caption).

strengths: Economical cell drawing; correct metric and area element
The 'grid bends, surface is flat' message is valuable

Edge labels are misplaced relative to the edges they name: from scripts/figures.py L119-120 (cell r 125-185 px, theta 0.5-0.9 rad, origin 265,325) the 'dr' label at (428,205) sits 34 px from the midpoint of the outer arc, which is an angular edge, and about 66 px from the nearest radial edge. 'r dtheta' at (380,151) is roughly equidistant from the outer arc and the upper radial edge. The figure meant to separate the two edge lengths does not clearly attach either label to its own edge. None of the three reviews noticed this.
Top-heavy layout with an empty lower half; no angle dtheta at the origin
The finite cell hides the limiting argument

assets.title: 08 Why a determinant belongs in the volume
assets.teaches: A linear map A sends the unit coordinate square to a parallelogram of area |det A|. For a Euclidean Gram metric g = A^T A, sqrt(det g) = |det A|, which motivates sqrt(-g) d^4x in Lorentzian geometry.
assets.pedagogy: A linear-algebra bridge from area scaling to the invariant measure; the caption flags the Lorentzian sign.
assets.physics_model: Illustrative linear map (square to parallelogram); the relation is exact.

strengths: Correct, simple bridge from linear algebra
Clean shapes
issues: The map's column vectors are not drawn on the parallelogram and the arrow is unnamed
Large empty gap between the shapes; a full-width sentence is baked into the SVG
Signed determinant vs positive area is not visualised

assets.title: 09 Acceleration without curvature (Rindler observers)
assets.teaches: Stationary observers in a rigid accelerating rocket follow hyperbolae X^2 - (cT)^2 = xi^2 in flat spacetime. Different heights need different proper accelerations, and Riemann curvature is zero, so varying clock rates are not proof of tides.
assets.pedagogy: Separates acceleration and clock-rate effects from curvature, before gravity is introduced as geometry.
assets.physics_model: Exact hyperbolae X = sqrt(xi^2 + T^2) for xi = 1, 1.65, 2.3, drawn at 105 px/unit horizontally and 85 px/unit vertically. The unequal scale puts the dashed null asymptote at about 39 degrees instead of 45.

strengths: Exact hyperbolae; clear flat-spacetime message
issues: The three coloured curves carry no labels (xi, proper acceleration c^2/xi, clock rate)
The null asymptote is unlabelled and not at 45 degrees because of unequal axis scales
All physical conclusions live in the text column

assets.title: 10 Do not confuse a route with its parameter (affine parameter)
assets.teaches: The same straight route can carry equally spaced (affine) or non-uniformly spaced labels. Affine parameters are related by lambda -> a lambda + b; a nonlinear relabelling adds a tangent-proportional term to the geodesic equation.
assets.pedagogy: Two rows of dots isolate parameter choice from path shape; almost no clutter.

assets.title: 11 Different components can describe the same arrow (moving basis)
assets.teaches: At three points on a circle a constant eastward field stays horizontal while the local radial and angular basis directions rotate, so component derivatives are nonzero even though the field is constant. The connection correction cancels them.
assets.pedagogy: Invariant arrow plus rotating basis. In the legacy book it was a collapsed reference inside the interactive moving-basis lesson.
assets.physics_model: Exact basis directions: radial (cos t, sin t) and angular (-sin t, cos t), checked against the rendered arrows at 25, 65 and 125 degrees.

strengths: Three identical eastward arrows make the invariant convincing
Basis directions are geometrically correct

Detached three-line legend; the oversized slogan footer outweighs the content
Unit basis vs coordinate basis is not distinguished visually

assets.title: 12 The connection cancels a false change (Christoffel symbol worked step)
assets.teaches: For a fixed eastward unit vector on the flat polar plane, V^r = cos theta and V^theta = -sin theta / r. Then nabla_theta V^r = d_theta V^r + Gamma^r_theta theta V^theta = -sin theta + (-r)(-sin theta / r) = 0: the Christoffel term exactly cancels the coordinate-component change.
assets.pedagogy: A worked algebraic step with the actual indexed coefficient (rebuilt after reviews criticised an anonymous 'relevant coefficient' card). It follows the moving-basis intuition.
assets.physics_model: Exact computation in coordinate-basis components; verified by hand (Gamma^r_theta theta = -r).

strengths: Correct explicit indices and derivative direction
Card framing removed; has a phone composition

Lots of empty space at 1000x580

assets.title: 13 A sphere remembers the loop (parallel transport holonomy)
assets.teaches: Carrying a tangent vector around the spherical octant P to A to B to P along great circles rotates it by 90 degrees, equal to area/radius^2 = pi/2 (angle excess). It is the signature of intrinsic curvature.
assets.pedagogy: The destination figure after tangent-plane, single-arc and loop steps. The caption warns that projected angles on the page are not the intrinsic angles. Paired with the 3D sphere scene and referenced in the transport lesson.
assets.physics_model: Orthographic projection of exact great-circle arcs on the unit sphere; rotation = enclosed area / R^2.

assets.title: 14 From 256 slots to 20 independent entries (Riemann component count)
assets.teaches: Antisymmetry in each index pair gives 6 pair labels (01..23). Pair-exchange symmetry makes the 6x6 pair matrix symmetric (6 + 15 = 21 entries), and the cyclic identity removes one, giving 20 independent components in 4D. These are not propagating degrees of freedom.
assets.pedagogy: A pair-index matrix with mirrored entries greyed. In the legacy book it was a reference inside the interactive 'pairs' curvature experience.
assets.physics_model: Exact combinatorics; the legacy interactive checked all 256 index choices (docs/second-figure-review.md).

Mirrored vs independent cells differ only by a subtle grey/violet tint
The cyclic Bianchi relation is not located anywhere in the matrix

assets.title: 15 Volume and shape ask different questions (Ricci vs Weyl)
assets.teaches: An isotropic squeeze (nonzero trace, Ricci-like) gives negative initial volume acceleration. A trace-free distortion (Weyl-like) stretches one way and squeezes another with zero initial volume acceleration.
assets.pedagogy: Two exaggerated cross-sections of an infinitesimal cloud. The caption distinguishes initial volume acceleration from later shear-induced volume change. Demoted to a reference inside the 3D cloud experience.
assets.physics_model: Schematic ellipses only (120x70 and a radius-72 circle against a radius-95 reference); not a solution of the Jacobi equation.

strengths: Careful caption wording about trace vs shear
issues: Overlapping circle and ellipse read like logos
No particles, velocities or accelerations; before and after carried by colour alone
A projected area cannot teach volume acceleration (the second review's own conclusion)

assets.teaches: Near a spherical mass the Newtonian relative-acceleration matrix has eigenvalues +2GM/r^3 (radial) and -GM/r^3 twice (tangential), summing to zero in exterior vacuum. At Earth's surface the radial value is about 3.08 um/s^2 per metre.

assets.physics_model: Newtonian tidal tensor of a point mass; 2 x 3.986e14 / (6.371e6)^3 = 3.08e-6 s^-2 (re-derived).

strengths: Quantitative, correct and unit-careful
Trace-zero vacuum statement links directly to R_mu nu = 0
issues: The boxed eigenvalue card outweighs the small particle cloud; arrowheads are oversized
'tangent' is listed twice without showing the second transverse direction
